newsitem.title: USA: Furniture Brands says Apollo to sell stake.
newsitem.headline: Furniture Brands says Apollo to sell stake.

text.p: Furniture Brands International Inc said Tuesday its largest shareholder, Apollo Investment Fund LP, has agreed to sell its stake in the company and give up control of the board.
Furniture Brands said it will spend about $175 million to repurchase about 10 million shares of stock and warrants from Apollo.

Under the agreement, the company also will file a registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for Apollo to sell 11 million Furniture Brands shares in a secondary offering, the company said.
After the transactions, Apollo will not own any Furniture Brands stock, the company said. Apollo's representatives will resign from its board.

"This transaction will eliminate any overhang caused by Apollo's large holding, will resolve any uncertainty about Apollo's exit strategy and will increase the trading liquidity in our stock," Mickey Holliman, president and chief executive of Furniture Brands, said in a statement.
Apollo has been a major investor in the company since 1991 and became its largest shareholder in 1992, it said.

Under the deal, Furniture Brands will buy back 10,842,299 shares of its stock beneficially owned by Apollo for $15.75 each. The price represents a 4.5 percent discount from the $16.50 closing price of the shares on Friday, May 23.
Furniture Brands also agreed to repurchase from Apollo its 290,821 Series 1 Warrants for $8.62 per warrant, representing the same $15.75 minus the $7.13 per warrant exercise price, the company said.
Apollo will sell 11 million Furniture Brands shares plus an underwriters' over-allotment option of 1.1 million shares in the secondary offering, the company said.
If the offering is completed at a price greater than $15.50 each, the repurchase price that Furniture Brands will pay for the shares and warrants will be reduced by $0.25, the company said.
